paragraphs: Inverclyde Council, through its health and social care partnership, looks after children in care across the council area, and its own fostering service is shown above with the independent agencies that cover Inverclyde.

The council has been open about the need for more local carers. In July 2025 it said the number of foster households had fallen to 20, from 34 in May 2020, and that some children in crisis were being placed in foster care outside the area because there were not enough carers locally. Its aim is for young people to be able to stay in Inverclyde.

To help, the Inverclyde Integration Joint Board agreed in 2025 to raise the foster carer fee from £195.75 a week, which had covered one or two children, to £350 a week for each child. The council also committed £700,000 for 2025-26 to redesign its children's services. Ask the team for the current rates.

Across Scotland, every foster carer should receive at least the Scottish Recommended Allowance for each child. For 2026-27 that is £177.68 a week for a child aged 0 to 4, £206.71 for ages 5 to 15 and £283.35 for 16 and over. Independent agencies set their own fees on top.

To foster in Scotland you need to live in the UK full time, have a spare bedroom and be at least 18, though some services ask for 21, and you can rent or own your home. The assessment, with preparation groups, checks and a fostering panel, can take 6 to 12 months. Speak to two or three of the services above before you decide.
